Name: Dennis Watson
Question: What do you think of the attempted assassination attempt of President Donald Trump moments ago?
Answer: I think the only reason Donald Trump is alive is because he got lucky. It looked like a complete failure of our security services. I hate to think of what may have happened had Trump been killed. (Photo credit: CNN.)

Name: Dennis Watson
Question: Military members, have you ever been accused of Stolen Valor?
Answer: No, I tell people that I was in the Air Force and they automatically know I haven’t stolen anything. People who steal valor tend to always say something ridiculous like, I was a SEAL, I was Delta bro, or at least an Army Ranger. Also, I have too many pictures of me in uniform that I could show someone if they really wanted to see them, although I know haters can say they were photoshopped. Anyway, it’s silly. I wouldn’t stand around arguing with someone about my military service. After all, they have no idea about your service record. So who cares? (On a “rotator” headed to Doha, before an onward trip to Baghdad. People who steal valor don’t usually claim service in a “cushy” service like the Air Force. Photo by author.)

Name: Dennis Watson
Question: What kind of firearms training do people receive in the military? What is the training like?
Answer: Generally, you receive training on all the small arms needed to do your job. For the great majority of people in the Air Force, this means the M16 or M4 series of rifles. As a security forces airman, however, my training included many more weapons on a course that is timed and scored for accuracy. I did such training with the M16 rifle, M4 rifle, M249 squad automatic weapon, M240 machine gun, M203 grenade launcher, and M9 pistol among a few others. Our training on the pistol range was memorable and I had the absolute best instructor teach me how to shoot a handgun for the first time. Later, that very same day, I qualified as a pistol marksman. I simply had no bad shooting habits to do away with. (An airman in the firearms training simulator (FATS). Image source: US Air Force). The same couldn’t be said of one of my classmates. Not only did our firearms training consist of live fire training, but training on a firearms simulator that consisted of “shoot/don’t shoot” scenarios. The idea of such training is to teach airmen when the use of lethal force is appropriate. These simulators were fun in that they use the actual firearm, but it is modified with a CO2 charge that cycles the weapon and produces simulated recoil. It isn’t loaded with any ammunition, but instead works as a fancy, but realistic, laser pointer. The system works in conjunction with short films that are projected on to a screen. The projector shows the location of any shots the officer fires by marking the screen with green dots. When it was my turn, I had accidentally caused the entire class to erupt into riotous laughter. I’d been given a shoot scenario where a man pulled a gun and pointed it at me. I rapidly fired off two shots. The scenario then froze and showed the location of my pair of shots on the perpetrator’s body. I’d shot him two times squarely in the genitalia. Being immature, everyone, including myself, doubled over in laughter. At least I didn’t miss! (“Fanning” in cowboy action shooting. Photo source: Dinosaur Cowboys). After we composed ourselves, it was then the turn of another airman. The first scenario played and he drew the pistol from his holster. It was a “don’t shoot” scenario, so he didn’t have to fire. The only problem was that he was drawing the pistol like a cowboy. While bringing the weapon up with his right hand, he was using his left hand to simultaneously cock the hammer so that he could fire the pistol in single action. Something that is quite obviously stupid. Our instructor told him to “knock it the f*ck off” and not do that again. The next scenario played and he did the exact same kind of cowboy draw of the pistol. This time it was a “shoot” scenario. While drawing, the airman simultaneous cocked the hammer with his left hand and then fired. It brought the hammer of the pistol down on the fleshy outer portion of his left hand and tore off a bit of it. He let out a shriek, dropped the pistol, and started bleeding everywhere. Everyone laughed even harder this time. Our instructor called him a “f*cking idiot” and sent him to medical.

Name: Dennis Watson
Question: What is it like to throw a grenade?
Answer: In one word: awesome! To start the day that we went to the grenade range, our instructors took us on a trail that went up the side of a small mountain at Camp Bullis, Texas. They didn’t tell us why we were on the trail or what was going to happen. After some time, we halted our patrol on a part of the mountain overlooking a small valley. Briefly, we saw a flash of light and then the sound of an enormous explosion which reverberated off the nearby hills. My first thought: holy shit! They took us to a gunnery range to watch the F-16 fighter jets drop a bomb! But no, it was just one of our instructors throwing an M68 fragmentation grenade. Needless to say, at least a few of us were quite terrified of actually throwing grenades after that little preview. I think that was the point of the demonstration. “Don’t fuck around when throwing these grenades, ya hear?” (Throwing practice grenades at Camp Bullis. Photo by author.) Thankfully, we first got to warm up by throwing practice grenades before moving on to the real thing. I never played much baseball, but I am rather good at throwing grenades. I find that having several ounces of explosive in your hand with a kill radius of 5 meters is plenty of motivation to make a good throw.

Name: Dennis Watson
Question: What are the best amazing tourist places with unique attractions in Mexico? Why are they the best tourist places?
Answer: I’m partial to the places that are a little off the beaten path, mostly in Yucatán region. Here are some of my favorites: Mucuyche. Small pueblo in Yucatán region. There’s a hacienda here that used to belong to the doomed Emperor Maximilian I of Mexico. Amazing, authentic food nearby, some of the best cenotes (underground rivers) in all of the Yucatán. This is an experience that should not be missed. (Hacienda at Mucuyche, photo by author.) Mérida. The capital of Yucatán state. It gets some tourism, but lives in the shadow of the more popular cities in the region like Cancun. Visit here to experience life in a culturally rich part of Mexico with food that is unique to the region. Be sure to visit the cathedral in the historic center. Get some cochinita pibil at a market and hangout at a cantina. (The incredibly popular La Negrita cantina. Get here early. Photo by author.) Campeche (City). Just one of my absolute favorite places in Mexico. I used to go here a lot when I just needed some peace and quiet and to eat good seafood. Some really nice boutique hotels near the city center. The historic center is very well preserved. (Historic center of Campeche. Photo by author.) (One of the hotels I used to frequent in Campeche. Photo by author.) Valladolid. A small town surrounded by jungle in Yucatán region. This town is famous for its unique smoked sausage. That alone is a reason to visit. Some nice hotels and a few historical buildings, but mostly a quiet and relaxing to visit. (City center of Valladolid. Photo by author.) Puerto Escondido. Popular beach town on the Pacific coast with surfers and some European tourists. Visit here if you like or want to learn to surf especially, but also if you want to go to a beach town that is still quite rustic and cheaper than most other beach towns in Mexico. Also, there are thousands of dolphins in the bay, they don’t mind if you swim with them. (Sunset in PE. Photo by author.) Izamal: Another small town in Yucatán that is almost entirely yellow. A very photogenic place. Visit the monastery and eat at the market. It’s not too far from Chichen Itza and worth a detour. (The monastery in Izamal. Photo by author.) Telchac Puerto: A sleepy town on the Gulf of Mexico with some of the best seafood. I would travel here many weekends just to eat the fish. You can also find a property directly on the beach for the weekend if you are so inclined. The prices are always reasonable. (Center of Telchac Puerto. Photo by author.)
